- Model tends to overestimate prices in early forecast windows, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast peaks by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots in the next 5–7 days; apply a downward correction of 3–8% for the following 7-day horizon.
- When sentiment is neutral or flat (all 0.00), model exhibits persistent bias toward higher prices; adjust forecast mean by subtracting 2–5% of recent 7-day average.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 30-day average, reduce by 5–10%.
- If true outcome shows a sharp downward trend after a spike, model often fails to recognize it; add a 3–5% downward bias for the next 7 days if sentiment remains flat.
- In absence of sentiment signals, model overfits to recent highs; use 14-day moving average as a smoothing anchor for 30-day forecasts.
